name: A run that stops without an answer persists an EMPTY assistant message instead of a stop reason — 2 measured cases, the real reason six shifts produced reports instead of fixes
description:
Created by ProjectManager shift 6 (2026-11-19 ~10:00Z). This is the defect behind the defect: every other card on `IT team` is downstream of it.

## What is measured (not inferred)

Agent runs that exhaust their budget mid-work do not fail — they succeed with a blank answer.

Case 1 — `8dfe4d74-7b74-416b-bb95-fc699272be73`, dispatched 09:53Z with `profiles: ["qa_automation"]` (a profile that demonstrably works):
- `message_count: 5`, `updated_at: 2026-11-19T09:54:48Z`, frozen across two `get_task` reads minutes apart.
- Last message role `assistant`, `content: ""`.
- No error, no partial answer, no tool-failure event recorded. The card looks "active" and is silently dead.

Case 2 — `4a30693e`, dispatched 2026-11-18 16:56Z, `profiles: []`: `message_count` 2 → 7, last assistant message empty. Originally (wrongly) attributed to missing ownership.

Control — same profile, same minute: `682e5f02` (created by the 09:52Z QA run) produced a full senior-quality deliverable. `5608c889` completed a real test cycle in 57 s. So the profile is not the variable: **the run shape is**. Long, multi-part briefs end blank; short single-purpose briefs end with output.

## Hypothesis to test (do not assume it)

The engine writes the assistant message record before/independently of the final response being produced, and the "stopped / out of rounds / no final answer" path never flushes a terminal message with a stop reason. Verify in the runner/loop code — candidates: the max-rounds / pause path (card `3d38db45` "cut at 10 tool rounds" is very likely the same code path), and whatever persists the assistant turn in the chat store.

## What to prove

1. The exact point where a run ends without a final assistant content, and what is written to the chat in that case (file:line).
2. Whether `run_status` / `run_state` on the chat reflect the stop (they should — a stopped run must not read as idle).
3. A minimal reproduction: a synthetic prompt that exhausts rounds, run twice, showing the empty persisted message.

## Acceptance

- A stopped run persists a terminal assistant message containing a stop reason (e.g. "stopped after N rounds: no final answer"), OR the run is marked failed in `run_status` with the reason — one of the two, not silence.
- The reproduction above is pasted as `command → output` / file:line evidence, before and after.
- `get_task` on an interrupted card shows the stop reason instead of `content: ""`.

## Notes / guardrails

- Use `project_read_file(pattern=...)` to find anchors — `project_locate`/`project_map` time out at 120 s (card `d8534b12`).
- Read-only investigation is fine for `software_developer`; the fix itself will need `project_write_file`/`apply_file_changes`/`qa_run_tests`, which is card `682e5f02` (the grant). Do not block diagnosis on the grant.
- Do not bundle the fix with the diagnosis: land the evidence first, in its own turn.
- Related cards: `bdae204a` (retracted ownership theory), `8dfe4d74` (case 1), `3d38db45` (round cap), `a5f95606` (same field-handling family — a value silently not persisted).

PM shift 8, 2026-11-19 15:15 UTC — THIRD measured case, and this one cost a milestone.

CASE 3 (new, today 15:05→15:15)
Task `a8cd259e-6c64-40da-8717-f686c927dbe8` (M1 closure evidence run, profile `qa_automation`).
- Dispatched `process_task(wait=false)` → child `cbdf9123-c851-4bba-ac51-4a3bcd515629`, status `queued`.
- Result on the card: `message_count: 3`, and `messages[2] = {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}`.
- No stop reason, no error, no partial text. The card looks "answered" in the UI and is in fact empty.

BONUS OBSERVATION on the same card: `messages[0]` and `messages[1]` are byte-identical user instructions — the initial instruction is persisted twice. If the empty reply is a stop, the doubled instruction is a separate (smaller) defect worth one line in the fix.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE PLAN (not just cosmetically)
The M1 milestone is "35 passed / 0 failed in one run". The run that was supposed to produce that number produced silence instead. Three per-file greens (6/0, 24/0, 5/0) exist, so the product is likely fine — but the milestone cannot be closed, and every future evidence card inherits the same risk.

ACCEPTANCE for whoever picks this up
- A run that ends without an answer must persist the stop reason (why: rounds, budget, timeout, provider error) as the assistant message, or at minimum as metadata on the message.
- Regression: a run stopped at the round cap leaves a non-empty assistant message naming the cap.

No engine processing requested here — this is a human/tech-owner decision on priority, not another expensive run.

PM shift 8, 2026-11-19 15:30 UTC — RE-POSTED: the first version of this note went through `update_task(comment=...)` and was silently dropped (`changed_fields: [priority]` only, `message_count` stayed at 2).

Recommendation: this card is P0, ahead of every other card on `IT team`. It now blocks a MILESTONE.

WHAT CHANGED TODAY
Dispatches to cards owned by profiles that are supposed to have the tools returned nothing:
- cases 1 & 2 — the two previously recorded cases (this card's own name);
- case 3 — `a8cd259e` attempt 1 (15:05): `messages[2] = {"role":"assistant","content":""}`, no stop reason;
- case 4 (candidate) — `a8cd259e` attempt 2 (queued 15:06, no reply at 15:27): either the same silent stop or a stalled queue. Both mean the card cannot be measured.

CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly
Every "done" on this board rests on an actor being able to reply. Today two of four cases sit on one card whose only job was to print five lines of pytest output — one command, and it got silence twice. Milestone M1 therefore moved 95 % → `onhold`.

ACCEPTANCE (two original items + one new)
- a run that hits its round cap or stops early persists a NON-EMPTY assistant message naming the reason and the cap;
- regression test covering that path;
- NEW: the combined 3-file pytest run on `a8cd259e` is the behavioural proof that the fix works.

Also still true from the earlier comment: `messages[0]` and `messages[1]` on dispatched cards are byte-identical duplicate instructions.

## MEASURED 2026-11-20 ~13:10Z — a THIRD failure mode, worse than the empty message: the run was never dispatched at all

Card `20821135` (capability probe) was created `2026-11-20 08:36:14Z` with `wake_at 2026-11-20T10:30:00Z` and `profiles: [software_developer, codx-junior-max]`. Read at 13:07Z, 2h37m after the wake:

- `message_count: 1` — only the seeding user message. No assistant message, empty or otherwise.
- `updated_at: 2026-11-20T08:36:27Z` — 13 s after `created_at`, i.e. **unchanged since creation**.
- `status: todo`, `progress: 0`.

So the 10:30Z wake produced **nothing at all**: not an empty reply, not an error, not a state change. That is a different defect from the two cases in this card's title (which have messages and a blank final turn).

### The pattern is not isolated
Overdue wakes with a stale `updated_at` on this board: `d8534b12` (10:00Z), `e816cc41` (10:00Z), `984cad11` (09:00Z), `7a8ffbc3` (09:00Z — this card did not re-run either), `ab4072b9` (09:10Z).

**Consequence for every report this project produces:** a due `wake_at` is not proof a run happened. Any shift report that says "dispatched" or "in progress" based on a wake timestamp is unfounded. Until this is fixed, `wake_at` is a scheduling intent, not evidence.

### PM action taken
No third dispatch (per the standing instruction). The probe's question was settled by direct measurement instead — see the comment on `20821135`: `project_write_file` is available, no command-execution tool is registered.

**This card stops being able to progress on its own.** It has now consumed 6 shifts of evidence collection and still has no owner and no profile. It needs an engineer with access to the scheduler/dispatcher — that is a management decision, not a task an agent can close.

### Third measured case + a second, separate symptom (ProjectManager shift 14, 2026-11-24 15:41 UTC)

**Case 3 — the M1 dispatch (`ed319cb9`), measured by me in this shift.**
`request_changes` was queued async at 15:32:56 with a 4-step instruction. The stored conversation ends with a single assistant message:

> "I'll start by locating the actual files and reading them before changing anything."

No further message, no tool call, no error, no stop reason. The card's `progress` stayed 0 and no file was touched. The run ended between the first sentence and the first action and the record gives no reason — the same shape as the two cases already documented here. Cost: the increment I consolidated in this shift has now to be re-dispatched a second time, which is exactly the mechanism that turned 13 shifts into 25 diagnostics.

**Second symptom, possibly the same root cause — message duplication.**
The same task stores its messages twice: index 0 ≡ index 2 (the create content) and index 1 ≡ index 3 (the `request_changes` comment). One queued request produced two identical user messages, so the engine may be re-entering the run with a doubled history. Worth checking whether the stop-after-first-sentence is caused by the duplicated turn.

**Reproduction for whoever picks this up:** create a card, queue one `request_changes` with `wait=false`, then `get_task` after ~60 s and count the messages. If `message_count` is even and the pairs are identical, the duplication is deterministic, not a race.

Fix priority: this card now outranks every gate fix on the board. While it is open, no dispatch on this board can be trusted to have done anything, and every "dispatched" claim a manager writes is false.

**Acceptance:** a dispatched run either produces a final answer or persists an explicit stop reason. `message_count` for a single dispatch is odd, never doubled.

### Case 3 confirmed by card metadata, not by reading the answer (ProjectManager, shift 14, 2026-11-24 15:5x UTC)

I re-dispatched M1 (`ed319cb9`) twice today with a one-step instruction. `get_task` afterwards:

- `progress: 0`
- `wake_at: null` — **the wake was consumed**, so a run did start
- `updated_at: 2026-11-24T15:37:18` — older than both dispatches, so **no new message was written by them**
- last stored message is still my correction comment; no assistant answer, no `STOPPED:` line, no error

So the shape of the failure is now precise: **the run consumes its wake, writes nothing, and the card silently reverts to `todo` with no schedule.** It does not even leave the empty assistant message reliably — sometimes it does (cases 1–2), sometimes nothing at all (this case). Either way the observable effect is identical: a dispatched card looks like an untouched card, so the *next* shift cannot tell "never started" from "started and died".

That is why 13 shifts produced reports: each shift re-read the card, saw `progress: 0`, and could not distinguish an unstarted card from a dead run.

### Consequence for this board
I am **stopping dispatches** into this path. Two async dispatches today produced zero output, and a third would cost another shift. `ed319cb9` is re-armed for an explicit human-visible check rather than another automatic attempt.

### What would let me prove it
A run that ends without an assistant answer must persist a stop record (reason, turn count, tool rounds used, last tool called). Minimum viable: keep the empty assistant message but append `STOPPED: <reason>` — that alone would have saved six shifts.

### CORRECTION to my previous comment on this card (ProjectManager, shift 14, 2026-11-24 15:5x UTC)

My comment two minutes ago said *"no new message was written by the dispatches"* and implied a fourth dead run. **That is wrong, and the evidence was in my own hands.**

While I was writing it, `ed319cb9` finished. Proof: its `description` was **replaced** during this turn by a 5-point summary the run authored itself:

> "2. Discovery ran out of tool rounds; the real repo root is `codx/junior/…` (not `api/codx/…`), and the gate logic lives in `codx/junior/quality/qa/gate.py` / `codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py`.
> 4. Correction issued before any edit: `project_tools.py` already contains `_filter_escapes_root()` with tests, so only M1 item 1 remains — no rewrite of existing code.
> 5. Honesty constraint: no shell in this runtime, so pytest cannot be run — the test file is written, not executed…"

So the run **worked**, respected the do-not-rebuild instruction, and corrected the repo root — which also explains my own `File not found` on `api/codx/junior/tools/qa_tools.py`.

### What this does to the defect's definition
It makes this card **narrower and more precise**, and it removes it as the sole cause of 0 deliveries:

| Symptom | Verdict from this evidence |
|---|---|
| Empty assistant message persisted | still real (cases 1–2) |
| Wake consumed, nothing written | **NOT confirmed** — the run wrote to `description`, `message_count: 7` |
| Run died mid-work | **no** — ran to a conclusion and summarised |
| "out of tool rounds" | **yes** — the run says so itself |

Two real sub-defects survive:
1. **The run's result lands in `description` (a field the board overwrites) instead of as a message** — so the next shift's `get_task` reads a stale/rewritten mandate and cannot see what the run concluded. That is why 14 shifts re-diagnosed the same thing.
2. **A run that ends "out of rounds" reports success and `progress: 0`** — no stop reason in `run_status`.

Acceptance should therefore be: a run that ends incomplete writes a terminal assistant message with `STOPPED: <reason>` **and** its findings as a message, never only into `description`.

I accept I filed a false fourth case. Corrected here rather than deleted, so the next shift does not repeat my inference.
